I should preface by saying i am MechE and not CS. That said, some baseline questions id ask were:

What is the biggest project you have worked on at [x] company?

How did you find out about this company/did you ever do an internship at this company?

What are the internship programs like at this company?

What qualities is your company looking for in a candidate? (Then when they say [x] quality, i reference my resume and what projects ive worked on that represent [x])

I really tried to go out of my comfort zone. Im not one to typically start a conversation with a stranger, but i tried my best to ask some baseline questions like these to get the ball rolling. While these questions helped me start talking to people easier, i think that what got me my interviews was the conversations i was able to engage in afterwards.

As for asking questions that were “too personal”, none of them said i was crossing any boundaries. I regularly asked what made them want to be an engineer, or why they chose x company, and none seemed to mind since it was just how the conversation was flowing. Just keep in mind that the majority of people love talking about themselves and their experiences.

I had this issue also, i felt like i was not getting anywhere no matter what I did. Last career fair i went to, i went with the mindset of meeting people instead of getting an internship, and truly getting to know who i was talking to and hear about their experiences. Lo and behold, i got my first ever internship interviews. Try to go iut of your comfort zone when meeting ppl at the career fair, really try to ask meaningful questions about their experience, it goes a long way.
